one_liner: Strict RFC 6455 WebSocket client/server crate for Tokio; ties or edges mongoose (C) on HttpArena small-message echo.
what_it_does: A WebSocket implementation built on tokio-util codecs: WebSocketStream is a futures Stream of Message plus a Sink of Message, over any AsyncRead + AsyncWrite. ServerBuilder::accept performs the HTTP/1.1 upgrade itself (httparse), ServerBuilder::serve takes over a stream another HTTP stack already upgraded, and ClientBuilder connects with optional native-tls or rustls. It is not a drop-in for a C or C++ library; it replaces tokio-tungstenite or fastwebsockets in a Rust service.
how_it_is_fast: Frame (un)masking dispatches at runtime (is_x86_feature_detected) to AVX-512, AVX2 or SSE2 kernels on x86-64 and NEON on aarch64, with more targets behind the nightly feature, and UTF-8 validation of text frames uses simdutf8. Payloads are Bytes, so echoing a message re-sends the same buffer without a copy, and since 0.12.0 queued frames are written with a single vectored write when the caller uses SinkExt::feed. In the HttpArena rows the messages are about 5-7 bytes, so none of the SIMD work matters there; the measured rows are dominated by one read and one write syscall per message (about 14.8 us of server CPU per echoed message at echo-ws-512 versus 16.4 us for mongoose and 14.2 us for ringzero-ws, derived from page data).
when_to_use: A Tokio service that needs a WebSocket server or client with strict RFC 6455 behaviour (UTF-8 and close-handshake validation, passes Autobahn without relaxations) and no permessage-deflate.
Many small concurrent connections where per-connection memory matters: 36 MiB at 512 connections and 98 MiB at 4,096 in HttpArena, below mongoose's 51 and 179 MiB.

Large binary or text payloads (16 KiB and up), where its SIMD masking and validation pay off; the project's own charts show it ahead of uWebSockets at 16 KiB (about 179k vs 120k msg/s at 10 connections, chart reading, first-party).
Projects already depending on bytes, tokio-util and http, or that want to bring their own TLS (rustls, native-tls, or none) and SHA-1 backend (ring, aws-lc-rs, openssl, sha1_smol).
Mature dependency choice: about 16.5 million crates.io downloads (7.6 million in the last 90 days) and 34 reverse dependencies including async-nats, iroh-relay, twilight-gateway and songbird.
when_not_to_use: You need permessage-deflate compression: the README lists it as unsupported.

Pipelined or burst traffic with the naive send-per-message loop: HttpArena's echo-ws-pipeline rows run at 0.30-0.42x of ringzero-ws, mongoose and proxygen (20.8M vs 59.0-68.4M msg/s at 4,096 connections), because SinkExt::send flushes every frame.

Lowest small-message latency per core is the goal: the hand-written C io_uring server ringzero-ws is 3-5 percent ahead on every non-pipelined row, and the project's own charts show uWebSockets ahead at 0- and 20-byte payloads (about 319k vs 290k msg/s).

Sharing one stream between a reader task and a writer task through StreamExt::split: the maintainers call it an anti-pattern and issue #128 (poll_close can hang after a completed close handshake) is open.
A non-Tokio runtime (async-std, glommio, monoio): it is built on tokio and tokio-util.

integration.dependencies: tokio, tokio-util, bytes, futures-core, futures-sink, simdutf8; one SHA-1 backend (sha1_smol, ring, aws-lc-rs or openssl) for client or server; base64, http, httparse for client/server; optional tokio-rustls or tokio-native-tls and an RNG crate (fastrand, getrandom or rand) for the client
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 (MSRV, edition 2024); the nightly feature needs a nightly compiler
integration.platforms: any Tokio target; SIMD masking on x86-64 (SSE2, AVX2, AVX-512, runtime-detected) and aarch64 NEON on stable, plus 32-bit ARM, PowerPC, s390x and LoongArch with the nightly feature; SIMD UTF-8 validation on x86-64 AVX2 and aarch64 only
integration.thread_safety: WebSocketStream is owned by one task; the implementation stores a single read waker and a single flush waker, and the maintainers advise against sharing it via StreamExt::split (issue #128, open).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — protocol-compatible with any RFC 6455 peer, so it can replace a mongoose or uWebSockets server process, but it is a Rust/Tokio API, not a C or C++ library

gotchas: Harness flaw against the library: the HttpArena server (frameworks/tokio-websockets/src/main.rs, contributed by the wtx author) echoes with ws_stream.send(msg), which flushes one frame per write; the crate has batched queued frames into one vectored write since 0.12.0 when SinkExt::feed is used, so the 0.30-0.42x pipelined rows reflect the bench code, not a ceiling of the library.

The headline 2-6 percent wins over mongoose compare files written in separate runs weeks apart (tokio-websockets.json 2026-08-28, mongoose.json 2026-09-21), every server uses 53-66 of its 64 pinned hardware threads, and messages are about 5-7 bytes, so the rows measure syscall and event-loop cost rather than WebSocket framing; treat them as a tie.

The HttpArena server also sets Limits::unlimited() and unwraps send errors under panic = "abort", so one peer reset during an echo would abort the whole 64-runtime process; the crate defaults (64 MiB max payload, 4 MiB frame size, 8 KiB flush threshold) are the safer starting point.
Message::close, Message::ping and Message::pong panic on reserved close codes or payloads over 123/125 bytes (since 0.11.0); validate user-supplied values before constructing them.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalogued web-and-serving entries it is the only WebSocket library; pick it over the raw Tokio or minima-sync HttpArena entries when you need a reusable, standards-strict WebSocket layer rather than a hand-written HTTP responder, and over wtx (wave 5) when you want the more widely used crate with strict compliance and pluggable TLS.
verified_claims_summary: In HttpArena (Threadripper PRO 3995WX, server pinned to 64 threads, gcannon client on the other 64 over loopback, best of 3 x 5 s), a contributed tokio-websockets 0.13 echo server built with nightly Rust, -C target-cpu=native and thin LTO echoed 2.17-4.20M small messages/s, 2-6 percent above the mongoose 7.23 C server (gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto) and well above proxygen, but 3-5 percent below the C io_uring ringzero-ws and at 0.30-0.42x of all three when 16 messages are pipelined.
status_note: Actively maintained (0.13.3 on crates.io 2026-06-25, last commit 2026-07-31), MIT-licensed, 152 stars but about 16.5 million downloads; copyable as a crate dependency, with three open issues including the split/poll_close hang (#128).
